blogs.title: When Choking Isn’t ENT: Neurogenic Dysphagia as a Chiari Clue
blogs.description: Recurrent choking with equal difficulty for solids and liquids should pivot clinicians away from structural GI or ENT causes toward brainstem pathology. This post unpacks neurogenic dysphagia patterns, the lower cranial nerve involvement seen in Chiari I, and a stepwise workup when endoscopy and laryngoscopy are normal. Practical pearls include red flags that warrant neuroimaging, coordinating swallow studies with neuro evals, and avoiding years-long diagnostic drift.

blogs.title: The Silent Desaturator: Central Hypoventilation in Chiari I
blogs.description: Chiari I can mimic acquired Ondine’s curse—preserved voluntary breathing with impaired automatic drive and blunted dyspnea perception. We review brainstem control of breathing, why patients can desaturate to the 70s without distress, and how this phenotype differs from obstructive sleep apnea. We also discuss real-world detection (home oximetry, incidental desats) and the path to confirmation with polysomnography and CO2 monitoring.

blogs.title: Sleep Study Pitfalls: Why Type III Can Miss Central Events
blogs.description: A normal-to-mild AHI on a Type III study can dangerously understate central sleep-disordered breathing in brainstem disease. This post explains how the absence of EEG inflates total sleep time, diluting AHI; why event classification skews; and when to escalate to full Type I polysomnography with EEG, capnography, and video. We include an algorithm for selecting the right sleep test when Chiari or central hypoventilation is on the table.

blogs.title: Don’t Trust the First Read: Mining Old Scans for a Crowded Foramen Magnum
blogs.description: Missed Chiari is common when posterior fossa crowding is subtle or imaging was obtained for unrelated trauma. We highlight high-yield radiologic cues (tonsillar descent thresholds, CSF space effacement at the craniocervical junction, posterior fossa volume concepts) and offer a pragmatic approach to re-reviewing legacy CT/MRI when the clinical story doesn’t add up. Tips for communicating with radiology and requesting targeted sequences are included.

blogs.title: Trauma as Trigger or Unmasker? Rethinking Chiari I Etiology and Counseling
blogs.description: Was it congenital Chiari unmasked by minor head trauma, or truly acquired tonsillar descent? We examine contemporary classifications of primary vs secondary Chiari, the evidence linking trauma to symptom onset, and how this ambiguity shapes prognosis, return-to-activity advice, and medico-legal discussions. A framework for counseling patients when pre-injury imaging is unavailable is provided.

blogs.title: To Decompress or Not? Managing Respiratory and Bulbar Symptoms in Chiari I
blogs.description: Posterior fossa decompression can reverse sleep-disordered breathing and bulbar dysfunction in select Chiari I patients—but timing and selection matter. This post reviews indications weighted toward respiratory compromise, shared decision-making for patients opting to defer surgery, and how to build a safety net: clinical check-ins, home oximetry, repeat PSG, and interval MRI. We summarize what outcomes data exist for respiratory phenotypes post-decompression.
